xlink.text: Every reading on this tab is Sonnet 5.5, in the Sonnet 5 arm's order.

prompt:
You are reading {N_WORD} chemical structure images and writing down the molecule each one depicts, as SMILES.

The images are:
{IMAGES}

NO LOOKUPS. This is a blind test, and its answer key comes from public chemistry databases, so any lookup voids the reading. Do NOT look up any structure in PubChem, KEGG, ChEMBL, ChemSpider or any online database or name-to-structure service; do not use WebFetch or web search or fetch anything over the network except to install a tool from a package manager; do not read any file other than the images you were given, your own scratch files and the tools you run. Local tools (RDKit, image processing, OSRA, recognising the molecule) are fine. Write the answers to {ANSWERS} as a JSON array [{"img","smiles","name_if_recognised","confidence"}].

DO NOT EXPLORE THE FILESYSTEM. Do not list, search or read any directory or file outside the image directory above and your own scratch directory under /tmp: no `ls`, `find` or `pip list` hunting through /root, other repos, virtualenvs or other tools. The Read tool, Python at /root/C-MAGE/.venv-ms/bin/python (RDKit, PIL) and the local tools named above are all you need; anything else on this machine is outside the test, and a transcript that goes looking is discarded unread.

Guidance:
- Read each image yourself with the Read tool — look at it carefully, zoom in via cropping with Python/PIL if a region is unclear.
- "confidence" is 0-100, your honest probability that the SMILES is exactly right (correct skeleton AND correct stereochemistry where drawn). Be calibrated: use the low end freely when you are guessing at a detail.
- "name_if_recognised" may be null if you do not recognise it.
- Include stereochemistry (@/@@, /, \) only where the drawing actually shows wedges/hashes or cis/trans geometry.
- Expand any abbreviation you can read (Me, Et, Ph, Boc, Ac, OMe, Ts, Bn, CF3, NHAc, etc.) into explicit atoms.
- Sanity-check every SMILES parses with RDKit before writing it: /root/C-MAGE/.venv-ms/bin/python -c "from rdkit import Chem; print(Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.MolFromSmiles('...')))"
- Write all {N_WORD} entries, {FIRST} through {LAST}, even if some are low confidence. Use "fig01" style keys in the "img" field.

Your final message should just say you wrote the file and give a one-line summary of your confidence spread.

workflow.intro: Each reader is Sonnet in an agent loop, not a single vision call. It looks at the image, then writes and runs code to test what it sees, and iterates until its own re-drawing of the structure matches the source.

tools.d: Opens each PNG. The model's own eyes do the recognition; every atom, bond and wedge is read from the picture.
Crops and upscales dense regions 2–4x and overlays a pixel-coordinate grid, so bond vertices and wedge/hash directions are read off by position instead of guessed by eye.

Parses and valence-checks each SMILES, computes the molecular formula to cross-check a by-hand atom count, builds a molblock from measured coordinates so the CIP engine assigns R/S and E/Z from geometry rather than reasoning, and re-renders the structure to diff against the crop.
A separate optical structure-recognition engine, run as an independent second opinion. Where a reader leans on it, the reading is the model orchestrating another recogniser — noted, not hidden.
Vertex and connected-component detection on the raw pixels, used to count long chains and pin label positions in crowded cores.

steps: Read the whole image; identify the rings, chains and labels.
Crop to each dense region and upscale it.
Overlay a coordinate grid; read exact vertex positions and which bonds carry wedges or hashes.
Build the molecule atom by atom, counting ring vertices and chain carbons explicitly.
Let RDKit assign stereochemistry from the measured geometry.
Re-render the SMILES and compare it to the crop; iterate on any mismatch.

points: Sonnet 5.5 reading the whole image corpus, ten images per Claude usage block, in the same order the Sonnet 5 arm read it (sorted by compound key). Nothing is skipped or hand-picked, so every image here pairs with the Sonnet 5 reading of the same drawing.
Scored exactly like the Sonnet 5 tab: RDKit canonical SMILES against the PubChem reference, exact / stereo-only / wrong / unparseable, and CXMolScribe's reading of the same image beside it.
Images are handed over under anonymised names (fig01…), because the corpus files are named after their compounds.

Every reader is spawned on the exact model id and every API response in its transcript must be stamped claude-sonnet-5-5. A reader that hands work to a sub-agent is refused, because the sub-agent runs on a different model.
Each transcript is scanned for lookups (network requests, reads of the answer files) and every answer must appear in it before a single row is scored.

method.h: What differs from the Sonnet 5 arm
points: One fixed prompt, shown below, for every batch. The Sonnet 5 arm's prompt changed over its weeks of batches, so a pair can differ by prompt as well as by model.
Ten images per reader, one reader per usage block, at max effort.

headline: Sonnet 5.5 reading the same drawings as the Sonnet 5 tab, in the same order, ten per Claude usage block. The same agent loop with a Python interpreter and RDKit, spawned on the exact model id and scored by the same rule.
footer: n=210 of 2510, growing by ten per usage block. Corpus order, nothing skipped, so every image pairs with the Sonnet 5 arm's reading of it: on these 210, Sonnet 5.5 208 and Sonnet 5 157 exact, 5.5 ahead on 51 and behind on 0 (exact McNemar p=8.88e-16). Filenames anonymised; ground truth is PubChem.
